text:
sasha.k: Heads up — I just found ~120 pg_dump files under s3://redwood-backups-prod/db-exports/ that appear to be uploaded without SSE-KMS metadata. Suspect this started after the backup-uploader serviceaccount policy change this morning.

ajay.r: Yikes. How did you notice?

sasha.k: Quick check: ran head-object on a sample. Output shows no ServerSideEncryption field.
```json
{
  "AcceptRanges": "bytes",
  "ContentLength": 8421345,
  "ContentType": "application/octet-stream",
  "LastModified": "2026-03-21T10:12:04.000Z",
  "ETag": "\"abc123...\"",
  "Metadata": {}
}
```

priya.m: That absolutely should have `ServerSideEncryption` and `SSEKMSKeyId`. Which IAM change rolled?

sasha.k: Looks like infra PR #3456 removed kms:Encrypt from the backup-uploader role as part of a least-privilege tweak. The uploader still had PutObject on the bucket so uploads succeeded but without KMS encryption.

lee_ops: Can you grep CloudTrail for PutObject events from that service principal and confirm timestamps? I can start an inventory job to list objects without SSE.

sasha.k: CloudTrail shows PutObject between 09:58–10:20 UTC from role arn:aws:sts::12345:assumed-role/backup-uploader/… Here are sample entries: `eventName=PutObject`, `userIdentity.principalId=AROA...`, no KMS fields in requestParameters.

oncall-bot: @channel Security oncall paged: incident created SEC-2026-0421, severity=high.

ajay.r: Immediate mitigation: 1) Revoke/rotate the temporary creds used by the uploader; 2) Re-run the uploader with correct kms:Encrypt permission in place to re-upload objects with SSE-KMS or copy existing objects to add SSE; 3) Quarantine unencrypted dumps and mark for rotate.

priya.m: For remediation copy, use server-side re-encryption via S3 copy to same key: `aws s3 cp s3://bucket/key s3://bucket/key --metadata-directive COPY --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id <key-id>` — but test on a single object first.

sasha.k: Agreed. I'll run a scan to list all keys lacking SSE and create a quarantined prefix `s3://redwood-backups-prod/quarantine/db-exports/` and tag objects with `security:unencrypted`.

lee_ops: Also add a CloudTrail/Config rule to detect PutObject without ServerSideEncryption header and trigger a Lambda to auto-quarantine in future.

ajay.r: We need an incident/notifications plan for customers who might have relied on those dumps being CMK-protected. Priya, can you draft a short notice and legal/PM loop?

priya.m: On it. Draft will include what happened, affected object prefixes, mitigation steps, and whether keys were exposed (initial look: no kms Decrypt logs, so keys not used to decrypt anything else).

sasha.k: I'll snapshot the list of unencrypted objects (object keys + size + putTime) and push to the incident ticket. Also adding a postmortem blurb: root cause = IAM policy change removed kms:Encrypt while still allowing PutObject. Fix involves policy rollback + tightly-scoped kms:Encrypt + pre-merge CI check.

lee_ops: Action items for follow-up: - add pre-merge CI lint that ensures changes touching backup-uploader role include a security review; - automate S3 inventory + daily check for SSE headers; - make uploading clients fail when KMS denies rather than silently upload without SSE.

oncall-bot: Status update logged to SEC-2026-0421.

ajay.r: One more — check if any downstream restore jobs consumed those unencrypted dumps. If so, revoke any derived credentials and re-run restores from re-encrypted copies.

priya.m: Will coordinate with support; tagging @legal @pm for incident comms.

sasha.k: I'll start the quarantine copy now on a small batch and report back progress (ETA ~ 45m for first 50 objects). :hourglass_flowing_sand:
